reason: Truncating a three-retriever interleave reduced HSTU-large candidate coverage.
Compressed NPZ arrays were decompressed on every batch and no epoch completed.
Second-last-event labels had been observed by the official HSTU autoregressive training split.
Random catalog negatives did not match the hard HSTU candidate distribution used at evaluation.
The protocol discarded the strong retrieval order and forced an uninitialized ranker to replace it.
Missing training targets were assigned rank 65 instead of using the final evaluation depth of 200.
Recency normalization scanned validation/test request times instead of fitting on training positions only.
